description.narrative: This action is designed in line with WASH cluster priorities and priority needs by the PWA, CMWU and will increase water productivity and access to safe drinking water for 10,000 individuals and domestic water for 22,000 individuals. This will include community engagement to foster the community’s sense of responsibility through the water user groups and monitoring committee to ensure transparency and accountability in the equitable access of water. This action will also contribute to prevention and reduction of public health risk through promoting good hygiene practices and supplying required kits to improve environmental and household level hygienepractices and community based environmental sanitation actions. In line with WASH cluster priorities, OCHA’s Post-Ceasefire Humanitarian Response plan to addressing Critical Needs in Gaza, Flash Appeal 2025 Priority Response and PWA Ceasefire Early Recovery and Restoration Plan: this action is designed to addresses the dire water and sanitation situations in North Gaza governorate through increasing production and access to safe drinking and domestic water supplies, improve house hold and community level sanitation and promote good hygiene behaviors and practices. Hygiene support includes the distribution of emergency hygiene kits and environmental cleaning kits. The action is tailored to mitigate water scarcity and prevent waterborne diseases, aligning with WHO recommendations for adequate water supply. This action acknowledges specific gaps, such as the need for household hygiene items, lack of storage capacity and solid waste management at community level, aiming to address these concerns in a comprehensive manner. While implementationis contingent on access and variables outside the scope of partners, Oxfam and BLDA will aim to deliver the assistance in the timeliest manner using Oxfam supplies. These include prepositioned items such as pipes and fittings, water storage tanks, desalination units and ongoing processes to transport supplies to Gaza from Jordan and Egypt. Oxfam also coordinates with IOM and UNICEF to access WASH supplies and ensure timely delivery and distribution of WASH items to the target population.

participating-org.narrative:
Beit Lahia Development Association (BLDA):
Establishment of the AssociationThe Beit Lahia Development Association (BLDA) was established on September 1, 1994, as a charitable, non-profit, and non-governmental organization, coinciding with the establishment of the Palestinian National Authority. The association was licensed by the Ministry of Interior under number (3071) and by the Ministry of Social Affairs under number (1212). BLDA emerged from the heart of the local community as a necessary responseto the need for an active institution to meet the community's requirements, address its interests and rights, and faithfully express its aspirations andhopes.
The responsibility of establishing the association was undertaken by a group of prominent figures and distinguished individuals from Beit Lahia who possessed high levels of expertise and qualifications. They gained the trust of the local community to serve the northern Gaza Strip in general and Beit Lahia in particular, without any form of discrimination.
Mission of the Association BLDA seeks to provide developmental and relief services and projects that meet the needs of the local community, focusing on vulnerable and underprivileged groups in northern Gaza. The association aims to empowerindividuals to manage and develop their available resources while promoting active community participation in planning, implementation, and decision-making.
Vision of the Association BLDA aspires to be the leading institution in building a democraticcivil society founded on freedom, equality, and social justice, contributing to sustainable development. Vision Statement:"To become the leading association in building a democratic civil society based on freedom, equality, and social justice, ensuring citizens' human rights and active participation with excellence and creativity to achieve sustainable development."
Strategic Goals Comprehensive Development: Contribute to the development of northern Gaza economically, agriculturally, educationally, socially, culturally, and environmentally. Community Empowerment: Enhance the participation of all community segments in planning, implementation, and monitoring the association's activities and projects. Effective Partnerships: Strengthen partnerships with local and international institutions and citizens to improve service quality and ensure genuineand sustainable development.
Fields of Work Education: Support educational processes through projects and infrastructure improvements. Health: Enhance health services in northern Gaza. Agriculture: Provide technical and material support to farmers to boost productivity. Humanitarian Relief: Offer emergency aid during crises and wars. Youth Empowerment: Build the capacities of young people and encourage their participation in community development. Women and Children: Advocate for women's issues, enhance their societal roles, and provide psychological, social, and educational support for children.
Approach and Distinction Since its inception, BLDAhasinvolved the local community in all stages of its operations, focusing on assessing its needs and priorities through a scientific and logical methodology. The association has maintained its operational independence and distinguished itself by transparency and integrity, which have reinforced the trust of the local community and partners.
